settings.dnsServerDomainHelp: The primary fully qualified domain name used by this DNS Server to identify itself.
settings.dnsServerLocalEndPointsHelp: Local end points are the network interface IP addresses and ports you want the DNS Server to listen for requests. The default values work for Windows but on Linux when you have multiple network adapters, you must explicitly specify the network adapter IP addresses here as the local end points.
settings.ipv4SourceAddressesHelp: The IPv4 source addresses that the DNS server must use for making all outbound DNS requests when the server is connected to two or more networks. Network addresses are also accepted.
settings.ipv6SourceAddressesHelp: The IPv6 source addresses that the DNS server must use for making all outbound DNS requests when the server is connected to two or more networks. Network addresses are also accepted. Note that this option will be used only when Prefer IPv6 option is enabled.
settings.localEndPointsNote1: Note! The DNS Server local end point changes will be automatically applied and so you do not need to manually restart the main service.
settings.localEndPointsNote2: Note! The source addresses configured above must be the IP addresses that are configured on the local system's network interface. When using source addresses option, it is also necessary to ensure that the system has a default route or a specific route for the source address to be able to reach the destination network. When source addresses are not configured, the IP address of the interface with a default route will be used as the source address.
settings.webServiceLocalAddressesHelp: Local addresses are the network interface IP addresses you want the web service to listen for requests. ANY addresses (0.0.0.0 & [::]) cannot be used together with unicast IP addresses. The web server uses dual-mode sockets by default so the IPv6 ANY address ([::]) works for IPv4 too. The default values work for most scenarios so, do not change these defaults unless you have a requirement for the web service to listen on specific networks. Configured unicast IP addresses will be included as Subject Alternative Name (SAN) in the self signed TLS certificate.
settings.randomizeNameWarning: Warning! Enabling the Randomize Name option may cause some domain names to fail to resolve due to their name servers dropping the requests or sending the QNAME in response with a different case causing mismatch. The DNS server can already detect DNS spoofing attack attempts and switch to TCP protocol automatically so its safe to not use this feature.
settings.defaultRecordTtlHelp: The default TTL value to use if not specified when adding or updating records in a Zone.
settings.defaultNsRecordTtlHelp: The default TTL value to use if not specified when adding or updating NS records in a Primary Zone.
settings.defaultSoaRecordTtlHelp: The default TTL value to use if not specified when adding or updating SOA records in a Primary Zone.
settings.defaultResponsiblePersonHelp: The default SOA Responsible Person email address to use when adding a Primary Zone.
settings.useSoaSerialDateSchemeHelp: The default SOA Serial option to use if not specified when adding a Primary Zone.
settings.minSoaRefreshHelp: The minimum Refresh interval to be used by Secondary, Stub, Secondary Forwarder, and Secondary Catalog zones. This minimum value will be used if a zone's SOA Refresh value is less than it.
settings.minSoaRetryHelp: The minimum Retry interval to be used by Secondary, Stub, Secondary Forwarder, and Secondary Catalog zones. This minimum value will be used if a zone's SOA Retry value is less than it.
settings.zoneTransferAllowedNetworksHelp: Enter IP addresses or network addresses one below another that are allowed to perform zone transfer for all zones without any TSIG authentication.
settings.notifyAllowedNetworksHelp: Enter IP addresses or network addresses one below another that are allowed to Notify all Secondary Zones.
settings.appsAutoUpdateHelp: DNS server will check for DNS Apps update every day and will automatically download and install the updates.
settings.preferIpv6Help: The DNS Server will use IPv6 for querying whenever possible with this option enabled.
settings.udpSocketPoolHelp: The DNS Server will use UDP socket pool for all outbound DNS-over-UDP requests when enabled.
settings.udpSocketPoolExcludedPortsHelp: Enter port numbers one below other to be excluded from being used by the UDP socket pool.
settings.ednsUdpPayloadSizeHelp: The maximum UDP payload size that can be used to avoid IP fragmentation.
settings.dnssecValidationHelp: The DNS Server will validate all responses from name servers or forwarders when this option is enabled.
settings.ednsClientSubnetHelp: The DNS Server will use the public IP address of the request with a prefix length, or the existing Client Subnet option from the request.
settings.ecsIpv4PrefixLengthHelp: The IPv4 prefix length to define the client subnet.
settings.ecsIpv6PrefixLengthHelp: The IPv6 prefix length to define the client subnet.
settings.ecsIpv4OverrideHelp: The IPv4 network address that must be used as ECS for all outbound requests overriding client's actual subnet.
settings.ecsIpv6OverrideHelp: The IPv6 network address that must be used as ECS for all outbound requests overriding client's actual subnet.
settings.qpmIpv4LimitsHelp: The maximum queries an IPv4 client subnet can make to DNS-over-UDP and DNS-over-TCP protocol services per minute on average based on the sample size. Set limit value to 0 to allow unlimited queries.
settings.qpmIpv6LimitsHelp: The maximum queries an IPv6 client subnet can make to DNS-over-UDP and DNS-over-TCP protocol services per minute on average based on the sample size. Set limit value to 0 to allow unlimited queries.
settings.qpmLimitSampleMinutesHelp: The sample size in minutes to be used for limiting queries per client.
settings.qpmLimitUdpTruncationPercentageHelp: The percentage of requests that are responded with a truncation (TC) response when QPM limit exceeds for DNS-over-UDP protocol service while the rest of the requests are dropped. A TC response will cause a real client to retry to DNS-over-TCP protocol service.
settings.qpmLimitBypassListHelp: Enter IP addresses or network addresses one below another that are allowed to bypass the QPM limit.
settings.qpmNote1: Note! Queries Per Minute (QPM) feature will limit requests from a client subnet based on its IP address and the specified subnet prefix lengths except for loopback IP addresses. The QPM limit configured will be compared with the average count from the sample size which means a client may exceed the QPM limit for a given minute but won't exceed for the given sample size in minutes. Rate limited clients will be listed in orange color on the dashboard top clients table.
settings.qpmNote2: Note! The configured TCP limits apply to the DNS-over-TCP protocol service as well as to the DNS-over-TLS, DNS-over-HTTPS and DNS-over-QUIC optional protocol services.
settings.ipv6Warning: Warning! Use this option only if this DNS server has native IPv6 Internet access otherwise it will affect performance. There are many name servers on the Internet that do not respond over IPv6 and thus enabling this option when you are running DNS server in recursive resolver mode (i.e. without any forwarders) may cause frequent operational issues with resolution that may result increase in Server Failure responses.
settings.udpSocketPoolNote: Note! Enabling UDP socket pool provides port randomization for all outbound DNS-over-UDP requests to mitigate spoofing attacks. It is recommended to enable UDP socket pool on Windows platform. On Linux, ports are fairly random and thus socket pool may be enabled if more randomization is desired. The DNS server can detect DNS spoofing attack attempts based on ID mismatch and switch to TCP protocol automatically.
settings.dnssecWarning1: Warning! Devices that do not have a real-time clock and rely on NTP when booting (e.g. Raspberry Pi), enabling DNSSEC validation will cause failure to resolve the NTP server domain name thus causing the DNS server to fail to validate all other domain names too due to invalid system date/time. To fix this issue, just create a Conditional Forwarder zone for the NTP server domain name (e.g. ntp.org) with forwarder set to this-server and Enable DNSSEC Validation option unchecked. This conditional forwarder zone will disable DNSSEC validation for the NTP server domain name and allow the device to update its system data/time on boot.
settings.dnssecWarning2: Warning! When forwarders are configured, DNSSEC validation will work only if the forwarders are security aware i.e. can respond to DNSSEC requests correctly.
settings.dnssecNote: Note! Enabling DNSSEC may increase delays in resolving domain names when the cache is initially empty. As the cache fills up, the performance will be normal as expected.
settings.ecsWarning: Warning! EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) option when enabled will compromises user's privacy since the DNS server will send the user's public IP network subnet to name servers or forwarders when resolving requests. When not using encrypted DNS protocols, this information can also be read passively by anyone on the network.
settings.ecsNote1: Note! EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) option allows passing the user's client subnet information to name servers or forwarders so that the response may contain IP addresses of servers closer to the user's geographic region. EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) option thus is only useful when the DNS server is hosted in a geographically different region compared to the users that are configured to use it.
settings.ecsNote2: Note! Enabling EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) option will significantly increase the DNS server's memory usage since the server will have to cache data for each client subnet separately. It will also increase cache misses since DNS server will have to resolve requests and cache them for each client subnet separately.
settings.clientTimeoutHelp: The amount of time the DNS server must wait before responding with a ServerFailure response to a client request when no answer is available.
settings.tcpSendTimeoutHelp: The maximum amount of time the DNS Server will wait for the response to be sent. This option will apply for DNS requests being received by the DNS Server over TCP, TLS, TcpProxy, or HTTPS transports.
settings.tcpReceiveTimeoutHelp: The maximum amount of time the DNS Server will wait for receiving data. This option will apply for DNS requests being received by the DNS Server over TCP, TLS, TcpProxy, or HTTPS transports.
settings.quicIdleTimeoutHelp: The time interval after which an idle QUIC connection will be closed. This option applies only to QUIC transport protocol.
settings.quicMaxInboundStreamsHelp: The max number of inbound bidirectional streams that can be accepted per QUIC connection. This option applies only to QUIC transport protocol.
settings.listenBacklogHelp: The maximum number of pending inbound connections. This option applies to TCP, TLS, TcpProxy, and QUIC transport protocols.
settings.maxConcurrentResolutionsPerCoreHelp: The maximum number of concurrent async outbound resolutions that should be done per CPU core.
settings.httpPortHelp: Specify the TCP port number for this web console over HTTP protocol.
settings.tlsPortHelp: Specify the TCP port number for this web console over TLS protocol.
settings.tlsCertificatePathHelp: Specify a PKCS #12 certificate (.pfx or .p12) file path on the server. The path can be relative to the DNS server's config folder. The certificate must contain private key.
settings.tlsCertificatePasswordHelp: Enter the certificate (.pfx) password, if any.
settings.realIpHeaderHelp: The HTTP header that must be used to read client's actual IP address when the request comes from a reverse proxy with a private IP address.
settings.webServiceNote1: Note! The web service port changes will be automatically applied and so you do not need to manually restart the main service. The TLS certificate too will be automatically reloaded when the certificate file's date modified property on disk changes. This web page will be automatically redirected to the new web console URL after saving settings. The HTTPS protocol will be enabled only when a TLS certificate is configured.
settings.webServiceNote2: When using a reverse proxy with the Web Service, you need to add X-Real-IP header to the proxy request with the IP address of the client to allow the Web server to know the real IP address of the client originating the request. For example, if you are using nginx as the reverse proxy, you can add proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; to make it work.
settings.webServiceNote3: The web service uses Kestrel web server which supports both HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 protocols when TLS certificate is configured. HTTP/3 protocol support is not available on all platforms. On Windows, it is available only on Windows 11 (build 22000 or later) and Windows Server 2022. On Linux, it requires libmsquic to be installed.
settings.webServiceNote4: Note! The web service will always bind to [::] local address for HTTP/3 protocol since this is how the libmsquic library is designed to work.
settings.webServiceNote5: Use the following openssl command to convert your TLS certificate that is in PEM format to PKCS #12 certificate (.pfx) format: openssl pkcs12 -export -out "example.com.pfx" -inkey "privkey.pem" -in "cert.pem" -certfile "chain.pem"
settings.enableDnsOverUdpProxyHelp: Enable this option to accept DNS-over-UDP-PROXY requests. It implements the PROXY Protocol for both version 1 & 2 over UDP datagram. It is mandatory to configure Reverse Proxy Network ACL below to allow requests coming from your reverse proxy server.
settings.enableDnsOverTcpProxyHelp: Enable this option to accept DNS-over-TCP-PROXY requests. It implements the PROXY Protocol for both version 1 & 2 over TCP connection. It is mandatory to configure Reverse Proxy Network ACL below to allow requests coming from your reverse proxy server.
settings.enableDnsOverHttpHelp: Enable this option to accept DNS-over-HTTP requests. It must be used with a TLS terminating reverse proxy like nginx. It is mandatory to configure Reverse Proxy Network ACL below to allow requests coming from your reverse proxy server. Enabling this option also allows automatic TLS certificate renewal with HTTP challenge (webroot) for DNS-over-HTTPS service when DNS-over-HTTP port is set to 80.
settings.enableDnsOverTlsHelp: Enable this option to accept DNS-over-TLS requests.
settings.enableDnsOverHttpsHelp: Enable this option to accept DNS-over-HTTPS requests.
settings.enableDnsOverQuicHelp: Enable this option to accept DNS-over-QUIC requests.
settings.enableDoh3Help: Enable this option to accept DNS-over-HTTP/3 requests.
settings.dnsOverUdpProxyPortHelp: Specify the UDP port number for DNS-over-UDP-PROXY protocol.
settings.dnsOverTcpProxyPortHelp: Specify the TCP port number for DNS-over-TCP-PROXY protocol.
settings.dnsOverHttpPortHelp: Specify the TCP port number for DNS-over-HTTP protocol.
settings.dnsOverTlsPortHelp: Specify the TCP port number for DNS-over-TLS protocol.
settings.dnsOverHttpsPortHelp: Specify the TCP port number for DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.
settings.dnsOverQuicPortHelp: Specify the UDP port number for DNS-over-QUIC protocol.
settings.certificatePathHelp: Specify a PKCS #12 certificate (.pfx or .p12) file path on the server. The path can be relative to the DNS server's config folder. The certificate must contain private key.
settings.certificatePasswordHelp: Enter the certificate (.pfx) password, if any.
settings.reverseProxyNetworkAclHelp: Configure the ACL above to allow requests coming from your reverse proxy server for DNS-over-UDP-PROXY, DNS-over-TCP-PROXY, and DNS-over-HTTP protocols. Enter IP addresses or network addresses one below another to allow access. Add ! character at the start to deny access, e.g. !192.168.10.0/24 will deny entire subnet. The ACL is processed in the same order its listed. If no networks match, the default policy is to deny all.
settings.dohRealIpHeaderHelp: The HTTP header that must be used to read client's actual IP address when the request comes from a reverse proxy. The specified header will be read only when the request IP address is allowed by the Reverse Proxy Network ACL.
settings.optionalProtocolsNote1: Note! These optional DNS server protocol changes will be automatically applied and so you do not need to manually restart the main service. The TLS certificate too will be automatically reloaded when the certificate file's date modified property on disk changes. The DNS-over-TLS, DNS-over-QUIC, and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols will be enabled only when a TLS certificate is configured.
settings.optionalProtocolsNote2: These optional DNS server protocols are used to host these as a service. You do not need to enable these optional protocols to use them with Forwarders or Conditional Forwarder Zones.
settings.optionalProtocolsNote3: For DNS-over-HTTP, use http://localhost:8053/dns-query with a TLS terminating reverse proxy like nginx. For DNS-over-TLS, use tls-certificate-domain:853, for DNS-over-QUIC, use tls-certificate-domain:853, and for DNS-over-HTTPS use https://tls-certificate-domain/dns-query to configure supported DNS clients.
settings.optionalProtocolsNote4: When using a reverse proxy with the DNS-over-HTTP service, you need to add X-Real-IP header to the proxy request with the IP address of the client to allow the DNS server to know the real IP address of the client originating the request. For example, if you are using nginx as the reverse proxy, you can add proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; to make it work.
settings.optionalProtocolsNote5: DNS-over-QUIC protocol support is not available on all platforms. On Windows, it is available only on Windows 11 (build 22000 or later) and Windows Server 2022. On Linux, it requires libmsquic to be installed.
settings.optionalProtocolsNote6: Note! The DNS-over-HTTP/3 protocol will always bind to [::] local address since this is how the libmsquic library is designed to work.
settings.optionalProtocolsNote7: Use the following openssl command to convert your TLS certificate that is in PEM format to PKCS #12 certificate (.pfx) format: openssl pkcs12 -export -out "example.com.pfx" -inkey "privkey.pem" -in "cert.pem" -certfile "chain.pem"
settings.tsigKeysHelp: The shared secret can be a base64 string or a literal string. Keep the shared secret empty if you want to auto generate a strong key.
settings.tsigNote: Note! You will need to configure these TSIG keys names for zone transfer in the zone options and in the secondary zone SOA record options separately.
settings.recursionAllowHelp: Enables recursion to allow this DNS Server to resolve any domain name.
settings.recursionPrivateHelp: Select this option if you want to support recursion only on private networks. Any recursive request from a public network will be refused.
settings.recursionAclHelp: Select this option to specify networks that must be allowed or denied recursion.
settings.recursionDenyHelp: Disables recursion so that this DNS Server works as authoritative only.
settings.recursionNetworkAclHelp: Enter IP addresses or network addresses one below another to allow access. Add ! character at the start to deny access, e.g. !192.168.10.0/24 will deny entire subnet. The ACL is processed in the same order its listed. If no networks match, the default policy is to deny all except loopback.
settings.recursionNote: Note! Disable recursion if you wish this server to act only as authoritative name server for the configured zones.
settings.randomizeNameHelp: Enables QNAME case randomization when using UDP as the transport protocol to improve security.
settings.qnameMinimizationHelp: Enables QNAME minimization for recursive resolution to improve privacy.
settings.resolverRetriesHelp: The total number of retries the recursive resolver must do per name server.
settings.resolverTimeoutHelp: The amount of time the recursive resolver must wait between retries.
settings.resolverConcurrencyHelp: The number of concurrent requests that should be sent by the recursive resolver to the name servers.
settings.resolverMaxStackCountHelp: The maximum stack count the recursive resolver must use for resolving a domain name.
settings.resolverNote1: Note! The DNS Server supports EDNS and thus all outbound recursive resolution requests will have an OPT record for it in the additional section. If a name server does not respond to a request containing OPT record, the recursive resolver will retry again without the OPT record when possible. This means that the number of retries attempted per name server can be Resolver Retries value multiplied by two for certain cases.
settings.resolverNote2: Note! The DNS server uses Epsilon-Greedy machine learning algorithm and will automatically learn which of the name servers are answering faster without errors and will use those name servers most of the time. Since each domain name has a different set of name servers, it may take a while before the algorithm learns about them.
settings.saveCacheHelp: Enable this option to save DNS cache on disk when the DNS server stops. The saved cache will be loaded next time the DNS server starts.
settings.serveStaleHelp: Enable the Serve Stale feature to improve resiliency by using expired or stale records in cache to respond when the DNS server is unable to reach the upstream or authoritative name servers to refresh the expired records before the Max Wait Time configured below.
settings.saveCacheNote: Note! The DNS server will attempt to save cache to disk when it stops which may take time depending on the cache size. If the DNS server takes a lot of time to stop then it may lead to the OS killing the DNS server process causing an incomplete cache to be stored on disk.
settings.serveStaleTtlHelp: The TTL value in seconds which should be used for cached records that are expired. When the serve stale TTL too expires for a stale record, it gets removed from the cache. Recommended value is between 1-3 days and maximum supported value is 7 days.
settings.serveStaleAnswerTtlHelp: The TTL value in seconds which should be used for the records in a stale response. This is the TTL value that the client will be using to cache the stale records.
settings.serveStaleResetTtlHelp: The TTL value in seconds which should be used to reset the stale record's TTL value in the cache when the resolver fails to refresh the data. The TTL reset causes the stale records to become valid again so that they can be used to serve requests normally. This reset effectively prevents the resolver from attempting to frequently update the stale records.
settings.serveStaleMaxWaitTimeHelp: The time in milliseconds that the DNS server must wait for the resolver before serving stale records from the cache. Lower value will ensure faster response at the expense of not getting updated data from the upstream. Setting value to 0 will instantly return stale answer without waiting for the resolver to fetch updates from the upstream.
settings.cacheMaximumEntriesHelp: The maximum number of entries that the cache can store. A relevant value should be configured by monitoring the Cache entries value on Dashboard and the server's memory usage to limit the amount of RAM used by the DNS server. A cache entry is a complete Resource Record Set (RR Set) which is a group of records with the same type for a given domain name. When a value is configured, the DNS server will trigger a clean up operation every few minutes and remove least recently used entries to maintain the maximum allowed entries in cache.
settings.minimumRecordTtlHelp: The minimum TTL value that a record can have in the cache. Set a value to make sure that the records with TTL value less than that stays in cache for a minimum duration.
settings.maximumRecordTtlHelp: The maximum TTL value that a record can have in the cache. Set a lower value to allow the records to expire early.
settings.negativeRecordTtlHelp: The negative TTL value to use when there is no SOA MINIMUM value available. Negative caching stores records in cache for NXDOMAIN and NODATA responses.
settings.failureRecordTtlHelp: The failure TTL value to be used for caching failure responses. This allows storing failure record in cache and prevent frequent recursive resolution requests to the name servers that are responding with ServerFailure or failing to respond.
settings.prefetchEligibilityHelp: The minimum initial TTL value of a record needed to be eligible for prefetching.
settings.prefetchTriggerHelp: A record with TTL value less than trigger value will initiate prefetch operation immediately for itself.
settings.sampleIntervalHelp: The interval to sample eligible domain names from last hour stats for auto prefetch.
settings.sampleEligibilityHelp: Minimum required hits per hour for a domain name to be eligible for auto prefetch.
settings.prefetchNote: The DNS Server cache auto prefetch option can keep eligible domain names from last hour stats "hot" in cache. Auto prefetch eligibility value can be decided by keeping an eye on the hits shown for last hour on the dashboard. Experiment with auto prefetch sampling interval and eligibility to get best results.
settings.enableBlockingHelp: Sets the DNS server to block domain names using Blocked Zone and Block List Zone.
settings.allowTxtBlockingReportHelp: Specifies if the DNS Server should respond with TXT records containing a blocked domain report for TXT type requests. This option also enables Extended DNS Error blocked domain report in response for requests that support EDNS.
settings.blockingTypeAnyHelp: Uses 0.0.0.0 and :: IP addresses for blocked domain names.
settings.blockingTypeNxHelp: Uses NX Domain response for blocked domain names.
settings.blockingTypeCustomHelp: Uses custom IP addresses provided below for blocked domain names.
settings.blockingAnswerTtlHelp: The TTL value in seconds that must be used for the records in a blocking response. This is the TTL value that the client will use to cache the blocking response.
settings.blockingBypassListHelp: Enter IP addresses or network addresses one below another that are allowed to bypass blocking.
settings.blockListUrlsHelp: Enter block list URL one below another in the above text field or use the Quick Add list to add known block list URLs.
settings.blockListUrlsNote1: For directly using block list files saved on this server, use the file:// formatted URL path. For example, on Linux the URL should look like file:///home/folder/myblocklist.txt and on Windows it should look like file:///c:/folder/myblocklist.txt.
settings.blockListUrlsNote2: Add ! character at the start of an URL to make it an allow list URL. This option must not be used with allow lists that use Adblock Plus format.
settings.blockListUrlsNote3: Begin a line with # character at the start to use it for comments.
settings.blockListUpdateIntervalHelp: The interval in hours to automatically download and update the block lists.
settings.blockListNextUpdateOnHelp: Click the 'Update Now' button to reset the next update schedule and force download and update of the block lists.
settings.blockListsNote: Note! DNS Server will use the data returned by the block list URLs to update the block list zone automatically. The expected file format is standard hosts file format, plain text file containing list of domains to block, wildcard block list file format, or Adblock Plus file format.
settings.proxyBypassListHelp: Enter IP addresses, network addresses or domain names to never proxy.
settings.proxyNote: Note! When proxy server is configured, DNS Server will use it for all outbound network requests.
settings.forwardersHelp: Enter forwarder DNS Server IP addresses or URLs one below another in above text field or use the Quick Select list to select desired forwarder.
settings.forwarderProtocolHelp: Select a protocol that this DNS server must use to query the forwarders specified above.
settings.enableConcurrentForwardingHelp: Enable this option to allow querying two or more forwarders concurrently instead of sequentially querying them in their given order. The DNS server will automatically select forwarders (based on their average latency) to query and use the fastest response it receives from any of them. If none of the selected forwarders respond in time, the DNS server will similarly select forwarders from the remaining ones and queries them till all are tried before giving up.
settings.forwarderConcurrencyHelp: The number of concurrent requests that must be sent when Concurrent Forwarding is enabled for resolving a domain name.
settings.forwarderRetriesHelp: The total number of retries the forwarder or conditional forwarder resolver must do per upstream DNS server.
settings.forwarderTimeoutHelp: The amount of time the forwarder or conditional forwarder resolver must wait between retries.
settings.forwardersNote1: Note! Forwarders are upstream DNS servers which this DNS Server must use to resolve domain names. If no forwarders are configured then the DNS server will use preconfigured ROOT HINTS to perform recursive resolution to resolve domain names.
settings.forwardersNote2: Note! The https URL scheme supports only DNS-over-HTTPS/2 and DNS-over-HTTPS/1.1 protocols. For DNS-over-HTTPS/3, use h3 URL scheme instead of https but note that there wont be any protocol fallback if the connection attempt fails.
settings.forwardersNote3: Note! The DNS server uses Epsilon-Greedy machine learning algorithm and will automatically learn which of the forwarders are answering faster without errors and will use those forwarders most of the time.
settings.loggingTypeNoneHelp: Disables all logging including error logs and audit logs.
settings.loggingTypeFileHelp: Enables logging errors and audit logs to the log file.
settings.loggingTypeConsoleHelp: Enables logging errors and audit logs to the console.
settings.loggingTypeBothHelp: Enables logging errors and audit logs to both the log file and console.
settings.ignoreResolverLogsHelp: Enable this option to stop logging domain name resolution errors into the log file.
settings.logQueriesHelp: Enable this option to log every query received by this DNS Server and the corresponding response answers into the log file.
settings.useLocalTimeHelp: Enable this option to use local time instead of UTC for logging.
settings.logFolderPathHelp: The folder path on the server where the log files should be saved. The path can be relative to the DNS server's config folder.
settings.maxLogFileDaysHelp: Max number of days to keep the log files. Log files older than the specified number of days will be deleted automatically.
settings.loggingWarning: Warning! Enabling query logging will significantly increase the log file size and use up disk space.
settings.enableInMemoryStatsHelp: This option will enable in-memory stats and only Last Hour data will be available on Dashboard. No stats data will be stored on disk.
settings.maxStatFileDaysHelp: Max number of days to keep the dashboard stats. Stat files older than the specified number of days will be deleted automatically.
settings.tempDisableMinutesRequired: Please enter a value in minutes to temporarily disable blocking.
settings.enableCheckForUpdateHelp: Allow the server to check whether a newer DNS Server release is available.
settings.ipv6ModeHelp: Controls whether outbound DNS traffic may use or prefer IPv6.
settings.udpBufferSizeHelp: Listener socket buffer size, from 8 to 65536 KB.
settings.locallyServedDnsZonesHelp: Serve RFC 6303 local zones and RFC 6761 special-use names locally.
settings.noStackTraceHelp: Log concise error messages without full exception stack traces.
settings.unixSocketHelp: The server process needs read and write permission on the parent directory.
settings.webServiceReverseProxyAddressesHelp: Only requests from these IP addresses or networks may supply the configured real-IP header.
settings.cspFrameAncestorsHelp: Controls which origins may embed the Web Console in a frame. Use 'none' to deny all.
settings.enableDohHelpRedirect: Redirect browser requests to the DoH help page
settings.enableDohHelpRedirectHelp: Redirect browser visits to /dns-query back to the DNS-over-HTTP help page.
settings.enableEcsSourceAddressHelp: Read the original client address from ECS on UDP and TCP requests from trusted proxies.
settings.flushCacheConfirm: Are you sure to flush the DNS Server cache?
settings.cacheFlushed: DNS Server cache was flushed successfully.
settings.blockListsUpdated: Block lists update was triggered successfully.
settings.tempDisableConfirm: Are you sure to temporarily disable blocking for {{minutes}} minute(s)?
settings.tempDisabled: Blocking was temporarily disabled for {{minutes}} minute(s).
settings.selectBackupItems: Please select at least one item to backup.
settings.selectRestoreZip: Please select a backup zip file to restore.
settings.selectRestoreItems: Please select at least one item to restore.
settings.quickAddHelp: Select a known block list to add its URLs to the field above.
